jobs.title: Warehouse Specialist
jobs.description_text: The Role The Warehouse Specialist is a highly organized and detail-oriented individual responsible for supporting inventory, coordinating shipping, and receiving operations to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and alignment with business objectives. The ideal candidate should be versatile, able to handle multiple tasks, and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment. This role involves monitoring inventory transactions, resolving discrepancies, implementing process improvements, and supporting cross-functional teams. The ideal candidate will have strong analytical skills, experience with ERP and WMS systems, and a keen eye for detail to drive accuracy and operational efficiency. This position will involve a balance of inventory management duties as well as active participation in shipping and receiving tasks. Key Responsibilities Maintain the integrity of inventory data within the ERP/WMS system, ensuring accuracy and real-time visibility for decision-making. Investigate inventory discrepancies, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to improve accuracy and efficiency. Process inventory adjustments, cycle counts, and reconciliations to ensure compliance with company policies and industry standards. Support ERP inventory module functions, including data entry, troubleshooting, and reporting. Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance inventory accuracy, warehouse organization, and overall supply chain efficiency. Train end users on inventory process

jobs.title: Senior Network Engineer
jobs.description_text: Role As Senior Network Engineer (Enterprise), you will design, deploy, and operate the network infrastructure that underpins Northwood's corporate facilities and hybrid cloud environments. This is a senior individual contributor role for an engineer with deep enterprise networking expertise who can build production-grade infrastructure from the ground up and maintain it to the operational standards required of a dual-use space communications company. You will own campus and facility network architecture, drive the implementation of zero-trust network segmentation, and ensure secure, high-availability connectivity across on-premises facilities, AWS GovCloud, and Cloudflare's backbone. You will work in close partnership with the security engineering team to ensure network infrastructure meets ITAR, CMMC, and government customer requirements. This role reports to the Head of Security. jobs.description_text: Role: As an Senior RF & Antenna Systems Engineer you will define and evaluate phased-array RF architectures for Northwood’s satellite ground-station network. You will translate mission and link requirements into antenna, aperture, beamforming, RF front-end, calibration, and tracking requirements, and evaluate how those choices affect end-to-end communications performance. This role sits at the intersection of phased arrays, RF systems, SATCOM links, and physical-layer communications. You will work closely with antenna, RF, DSP/communications, digital, mechanical, manufacturing, software, and operations teams to ensure that the complete ground-station system achieves its required link performance. As our founding PCB Designer, you won't just be routing traces; you will partner closely with our Electrical, RF, and Antenna engineers from concept to production, setting the technical bar for layout expertise and building the foundation for a team that delivers hardware known for its reliability, scalability, and cost. jobs.title: Product Security Manager
jobs.description_text: Role As Product Security Lead, you will own the security of Northwood's software and systems from design through deployment. This is a senior technical leadership role for an engineer with deep expertise across the full product security lifecycle — from threat modeling and secure architecture review to penetration testing, vulnerability management, and the cryptographic foundations that protect mission-critical space communications. You will embed security into every stage of our software development lifecycle, build and mature our application security program, and ensure that the products Northwood delivers to government and commercial customers meet the most demanding security requirements in the industry. This role partners closely with product and infrastructure engineering teams and reports to the Head of Security. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer- Fleet Operations & Reliability
jobs.description_text: Role: Northwood is building a global network of next-generation ground stations, and we're looking for a Fleet Operations & Reliability Engineer who is equal parts technical expert, field operator, and builder. You will be the first line of defense for all operations on our network - the extreme owner of uptime and performance for our deployed hardware worldwide. Your work will span most technical disciplines at the company giving you broad technical exposure across the stack, and will require you to build consensus across multiple teams. Day-to-day, you'll move between operating our hardware - interpreting live telemetry, driving incident response, analyzing performance data - and leading field campaigns to deploy, diagnose, and upgrade hardware at remote sites. As you build deep knowledge of our systems, you'll be positioned to drive scalable, automated monitoring and response systems. jobs.title: Head of AI
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Osmo is building the first computer that can smell. Olfactory Intelligence (OI) is the model suite behind that: it predicts how a molecule or a mixture will smell, generates new formulas from a creative brief, and now powers commercial products for some of the largest consumer goods companies in the world. It runs on 5.4M+ human sniff annotations, 100M+ mass spectral readings, and a molecule library in the billions, data no one else has. We are hiring a Head of Applied AI to own the team that builds these models. You will lead the ML engineers and research scientists, set the roadmap and the quality bar, and own the path from research notebook to production API. jobs.title: Research Scientist/Research Engineer, Materials Data
jobs.description_text: About the Role At Periodic Labs, we are automating scientific research in materials discovery; the data we collect, and how we represent it, is what makes this possible. We are hiring a materials scientist to work across the entire process: to find where our agents and data fail, and to fix those failures at the source. This is a hybrid research and infrastructure role. Roughly half your time will be spent working directly with our experimental and computational scientists, building agents and tools that solve active research problems. The other half will be spent improving the data those agents depend on. This role requires domain depth, not just data engineering skill. You need to know, for example, what metadata actually matters for a given characterization technique. The research half of the role keeps you grounded in the problems we are actually using LLMs to solve, so the schemas you build serve real research rather than an abstraction of it. The work demands attention to detail and a willingness to get into the weeds: to meticulously read, understand, and improve our data. You'll be as much a materials scientist doing research as the person who makes our agentic harness actually work. What You'll Do - Work directly with lab scientists and the computational team on active research problems, staying close to the actual bottlenecks LLM agents are meant to solve. - Investigate agent traces to identify data errors and agentic failure modes, and eliminate them at the source.

The DS guides customer and Rivet collaboration, aligning teams and deployment plans to meet mutual objectives. The strategist is responsible for analyzing customer conditions, understanding data insights, and developing actionable plans to achieve desired outcomes. Additionally, the DS anticipates potential challenges, devising solutions to mitigate risks – or to achieve win/win competitive advantage. As a relationship manager, the DS serves as a liaison between technical teams and customer stakeholders, facilitating clear understanding of project goals and progress. The strategist monitors deployment activities, provides regular updates, and ensures fidelity to agreed timelines and milestones. This role favors strong planning skills, acumen for technology breakthroughs with large customers, and a bias toward iterative action. At Rivet, the DS is uniquely positioned to create long-term value with customers trusting us with their most strategic projects. In addition to deployment execution, the DS plays a key role in shaping new business opportunities. This includes partnering with commercial and technical teams to scope prospective engagements, contribute to technical and programmatic proposals, and translate customer needs into compelling, executable plans. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Location & Motion (Inertial Navigation / GNSS)
jobs.description_text: Summary We’re looking for an experienced engineer to own the navigation and positioning stack for Rivet’s head-worn and body-worn systems. You will be responsible for turning inertial and GNSS sensor data into a robust, continuous estimate of position and orientation across challenging real-world environments. This includes sensor calibration and characterization, inertial navigation, GNSS integration, and the estimation algorithms that bring these inputs together. You will work closely with our perception team to define how navigation and visual tracking complement one another and provide a stable experience to downstream systems. This is a highly hands-on role spanning algorithms, embedded software, hardware integration, laboratory testing, and field validation. Responsibilities - Own the end-to-end 9-axis inertial sensing system, including accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer calibration, synchronization, coordinate frames, and attitude estimation. - Develop robust heading and inertial navigation solutions that account for sensor errors, environmental disturbances, temperature variation, and platform effects. - Own GNSS integration and performance, including receiver configuration, raw measurement analysis, signal quality characterization, and resilience to degraded or unreliable positioning environments. - Design and maintain the navigation fusion estimator, combining inertial, GNSS, and other available measurements into a continuous position, velocity, and attitude

We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. jobs.description_text: About this Role We are building a Group 5 autonomous aircraft and driving it to first flight. We are in detailed design with tooling in work, and we are looking for a structures design engineer to own parts on that aircraft from concept through first article. You will design and size real hardware: control surfaces, ribs and spars, frames, doors and access panels, fittings and joints. You will take your parts all the way out, through analysis, drawings, vendor coordination, first article, and the fixes that come after. Our structures lead sets the architecture and the design approach. Inside that, your parts are yours. This is a role for someone who wants to design more and coordinate less. You will be in CAD and in FEA most days, and in the shop the rest of them. The aircraft is small enough as an organization that the person who draws a part is the person who sees it come off the tool, and finds out the same week whether the call they made was right. jobs.title: Spring 2027 Legal Intern, Criminal Law Reform Project
jobs.description_text: About the Role The ACLU seeks a Spring Legal Intern in the Criminal Law Reform Project of the ACLU’s National office. This is a hybrid position based out of our National Office in New York, NY. Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated legal students and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship. The Team: The Criminal Law Reform Project advocates for the constitutional and civil rights of those impacted by criminal legal systems. We use litigation and advocacy to confront systemic government conduct that fuels the carceral state and police abuse, and oppresses people based on race, class, and other characteristics. CLRP does this work because everyone suspected, accused, or convicted of a crime deserves dignity, fairness, and an opportunity to thrive. Ultimately, we seek to shift power to under-resourced communities and to elevate approaches to justice and safety that advance fundamental rights for all. The Project’s current priorities are combatting police violence while bolstering individual rights against police authority; protecting the fundamental right to pretrial liberty; eliminating excessive conditions of post release supervision; and creating robust public defense systems to guarantee the constitutional right to counsel. CLRP works closely with the ACLU’s National Political Advocacy Department, our Communications Department, and our affiliates to advance an affirmative vision for criminal legal system reform. jobs.description_text: The Community You Will Join: Guest & Host Technology builds the end-to-end experience that connects people around the world. Our team owns the identity and privacy layer beneath that experience: the systems that determine who can see what about whom, in what context, and why. Get this layer wrong and it either breaks trust or breaks the product; our job is to make sure it does neither. You'll be reasoning about relationship-scoped access (who's allowed to see this, given the specific context they're asking from), and building systems that other teams across the company depend on to do the same correctly. You'll work across true backend fundamentals: service architecture, data modeling, authorization logic, and migration tooling that needs to run safely at Airbnb's scale without breaking the dozens of teams who consume these systems. jobs.description_text: The Community You Will Join The Online Data organization helps Airbnb's builders create real-time data experiences through intuitive data interfaces and tools, with no database expertise required. Within Online Data, the Transactional Storage Services team owns the core storage infrastructure behind Airbnb's online data systems. We design, build, and operate a new source-of-truth, horizontally scalable, open-source NewSQL database running on stateful Kubernetes. It holds Airbnb's critical user, listing, and financial data. You'll join the Database Kernel team, which owns performance, reliability, and stability for Airbnb's NewSQL engine at scale. The team's work centers on the storage layer and query execution engine, and also covers consensus and shard management. In this role you'll dig into database internals to diagnose and fix SQL latency and availability issues. You'll also work closely with our open-source database vendor on root cause analysis and upstream contributions. Analyze query plans and execution paths (planning, optimization, operators, and distributed execution) to find and fix sources of SQL latency.
